payload.name: Preserve explicit evaluative claims in extraction
payload.description: When extracting memory candidates from a message with both descriptive details and explicit positive/negative assessments, promises, or recommendations, include the explicit evaluative claim in the candidate content.
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker makes an explicit evaluative or attitudinal claim (e.g., a promise, warning, or recommendation), preserve that claim as part of the candidate content rather than only summarizing the descriptive context.

Before finalizing an ADD, verify that each distinct explicit claim in the source message is represented in a candidate; if one is missing, expand the candidate or create a separate memory anchored to the same source.

solves: During construction extraction, when a message contains both a descriptive summary and an explicit evaluative or attitudinal statement (such as a promise, recommendation, or prediction), the candidate should preserve that explicit claim instead of paraphrasing only the surrounding description. This applies to any future extraction where a distinct direct statement would otherwise be lost; it does not require storing every subjective phrase.
